title: Example Lore: The Ashen Coast
body:
# Example Lore: The Ashen Coast

This worked example demonstrates correct D&D lore prose: voice, tense usage, DM/player split, and the balance between evocative description and practical usability. The example shows both the produced prose and annotated commentary explaining the choices.

---

## Produced Prose — Setting Overview

The Ashen Coast is a twenty-mile stretch of dead shoreline north of the Vel'than estuary where nothing has grown in three hundred years. The sand is grey-white and fine as chalk. The sea here does not crash — it slides in and retreats without sound, leaving behind a residue that locals call the Salt of Endings. Fishing villages along the coast abandoned their harbors two generations ago. The ones who stayed did not leave willingly.

The Coast is not a ruin. It is a wound that has not healed and shows no sign of healing. The architecture of the abandoned villages is intact. The docks are structurally sound. The boats are still tied. Nothing rots here. Nothing grows. The fish in the shallows are alive but will not come to shore.

**[ANNOTATION — Voice]:** This is the lore-dm voice: matter-of-fact, specific, no flowery language. Each sentence establishes a fact with sensory grounding. "Fine as chalk" is a texture, not a decoration. "Will not come to shore" implies something the DM can use without over-explaining it.

---

## Produced Prose — History

In 1,287 by the Common Reckoning, the Vel'than Convocation attempted a mass binding ritual to contain the escaped aspect known as the Hollow Tide. They failed. The ritual did not destroy the Hollow Tide — it anchored it. The entity is still present in the Coast, distributed across the sand and sea rather than embodied. The Convocation mages who performed the ritual are also still present, though not in a form their families would recognize.

The event is called the Silencing in local records. Scholars outside the region refer to it as the Vel'than Catastrophe. The Convocation's descendant institutions dispute both names and deny culpability. [DM ONLY: The Convocation's current leadership knows exactly what happened and has spent three centuries ensuring that no one who could undo the anchoring survives long enough to try.]

**[ANNOTATION — Tense and DM/Player split]:** Current world state ("is still present") uses present tense. Historical events ("attempted," "failed," "anchored") use past tense. The [DM ONLY] block contains the actionable secret — the player-facing version of this document omits that paragraph entirely. The secret is not hidden in vague language — it is clearly bracketed.

---

## Produced Prose — Adventure Hooks

1. A cartographer hired by the Convocation's successor institutions is mapping the extent of the silent zone. She has not reported back in six weeks. Her last message mentioned something following her at low tide.
2. A local fisherman is offering a year's wages to anyone who will retrieve the body of his wife from the village of Karath-on-Shore. She died three days ago. Her body is still visible through the window of their cottage.
3. A researcher from the Artificers' Academy believes the Ashen Coast contains the largest concentration of stable ambient binding energy in the known world. She wants to harvest it. She has not asked what it is binding.

**[ANNOTATION — Hook structure]:** Each hook names a specific person with a specific problem arising from the lore. Hook 1 uses the DM-only secret as its engine without revealing it. Hook 2 creates immediate dread from the non-rotting detail established in the overview. Hook 3 uses a named institution and creates conflict from ignorance rather than malice.

---

## Player-Facing Version Note

A player-facing handout version of this entry would include: the setting overview (minus any specific named details the DM wants to reveal gradually), the non-bracketed portions of the history, and hooks 1 and 2 reframed as local rumors rather than direct DM information. The [DM ONLY] paragraph in the history section would be entirely omitted.
